source_evidence: Any promise to repay some or all of the money you invest will depend on the creditworthiness of the issuer of the note—meaning you could lose all of your money if the issuer of your note goes bankrupt.
answer: Structured notes with principal protection are not risk-free. A promise to repay some or all of your investment depends on the note issuer’s creditworthiness. If the issuer goes bankrupt, you could lose all of your money, even if the note’s name suggests principal protection.
